answer: According to arXiv 2503.18983, the right to life under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) expressly protects individuals from "arbitrary" deprivations of life. An "arbitrary" deprivation of life is defined as involving an interference that is (1) not prescribed by law, (2) disproportionate to the ends sought, and (3) not necessary in the circumstances of the case considering the availability of less harmful means.
